title: The Second Letter of Peter Timeline
sub: Eyewitness Testimony · False Teachers and the Coming Day
desc: Written as Peter sensed his death approaching, grounding its authority in personal eyewitness of the Transfiguration before turning to a relentless warning against false teachers and a direct answer to those mocking the promise of Christ's return.

eras.label: Era One · 2 Peter 1
eras.name: Confirming Your Calling — Eyewitnesses of His Majesty
eras.dates: Written, by Peter's own account, as he sensed his death approaching: a last reminder grounded in something he personally saw and heard

events.title: Partakers of the Divine Nature
events.detail: Peter opens with one of the boldest statements in the New Testament: God's power has granted everything needed for life and godliness, through promises so great believers become 'partakers of the divine nature,' escaping the world's corruption.

verses.text: “He has granted to us His precious and magnificent promises, so that by them you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world by lust.”

events.title: A Ladder of Virtues: Make Your Calling Sure
events.detail: A chain of seven qualities, each meant to build on the last, faith to moral excellence to knowledge to self-control to perseverance to godliness to brotherly kindness to love, as the path to a calling made sure.

verses.text: “Be all the more diligent to make your calling and choosing sure; for in doing these things, you will never stumble.”

events.title: Peter's Approaching Death: A Reminder Before He Departs
events.detail: Peter writes with real urgency, aware that his own death is near, wanting to leave behind a reminder sturdy enough that the church could recall it long after he was gone.

verses.text: “Knowing that the laying aside of my earthly dwelling is imminent, as also our Lord Jesus Christ has indicated to me.”

events.title: Eyewitnesses of His Majesty: A Voice From the Holy Mountain
events.detail: Peter grounds his authority not in clever invented myths but in personal experience: he was there on the mountain and heard the voice declare Jesus God's beloved Son, and points beyond even that to the even more certain prophetic word of Scripture.

verses.text: “We did not make known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, following cleverly devised myths, but being eyewitnesses of His majesty.”
“No prophecy of Scripture comes by one's own interpretation… men being moved by the Holy Spirit spoke from God.”

eras.label: Era Two · 2 Peter 2
eras.name: False Teachers and Their Coming Destruction
eras.dates: A relentless chapter naming Old Testament precedents for judgment, one after another, applied directly to teachers infiltrating the church

events.title: False Teachers Will Secretly Introduce Destructive Heresies
events.detail: Just as Israel had false prophets, the church will have false teachers who deny Christ and exploit believers with fabricated words for profit: their judgment, Peter warns, is already in motion.

verses.text: “False teachers among you, who will secretly introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them, bringing swift destruction upon themselves.”

events.title: Precedents for Judgment: Fallen Angels, the Flood, Sodom and Gomorrah
events.detail: Three Old Testament examples stack up to prove God both judges the wicked and rescues the righteous: angels cast into chains, Noah preserved through the flood, and Lot rescued from Sodom and Gomorrah.

verses.text: “The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment.”

events.title: The Character of the False Teachers: Balaam's Donkey and a Dog's Vomit
events.detail: An escalating, almost violent description of the false teachers as unreasoning animals and slaves of their own corruption, compared to Balaam, rebuked by a talking donkey, and closed with two blunt proverbs about returning to what one has escaped.

verses.text: “A dog returns to its own vomit,’ and, ‘A sow, after washing, returns to wallowing in the mire.’”

eras.label: Era Three · 2 Peter 3
eras.name: The Day of the Lord Will Come Like a Thief
eras.dates: A direct answer to scoffers asking why Christ still hadn't returned, and a promise of new heavens and a new earth

events.title: Scoffers Will Come, Denying the Promise
events.detail: Peter predicts mockers who will ask why nothing has changed since creation, and answers them by pointing back to the flood: proof the world has already been remade by judgment once, and will be again by fire.

verses.text: “Where is the promise of His coming? For since the fathers fell asleep, all continues just as it was from the beginning of creation.”

events.title: A Thousand Years Like One Day: The Day of the Lord Comes Like a Thief
events.detail: Apparent delay is reframed as patience, not slowness: God's timescale isn't human timescale, and his forbearance exists so more people have opportunity to repent before the day arrives suddenly, like a thief.

verses.text: “The Lord is not slow about His promise, as some consider slowness, but is patient toward you, not willing for any to perish but for all to come to repentance.”

events.title: New Heavens and a New Earth: A Nod to Paul's Difficult Letters
events.detail: Knowing the present order will be dissolved, believers are urged toward holy conduct while awaiting new heavens and a new earth, and Peter closes with a striking, early acknowledgment that Paul's own letters already circulated as authoritative, if sometimes hard to understand, Scripture.

verses.text: “According to His promise we are looking for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.”

“Our beloved brother Paul, according to the wisdom given him, wrote to you… in which are some things hard to understand, which the untaught and unstable distort, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures.” — an early witness to Paul's letters already being read as Scripture.
